chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Qur'an that Jibril (peace be upon him) brought to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was seventeen thousand verses.
ai.seo_question: How many verses were in the original Qur'an according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of al-Saduq, asserts that the total number of verses in the Qur'an was 17,000, a figure often cited in Shia hadith literature to support the theory of textual expansion or the existence of verses removed from the standard mushaf. This count contrasts with the Uthmanic codex's approximate 6,200 verses, highlighting the scholarly debate regarding the completeness of the current text versus the full revelation received by the Prophet. The distinction underscores the Shia perspective on the Qur'an's multifaceted nature, encompassing both the recited text and the deeper, esoteric meanings.

en.ammaar-muslim: [3/1564] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Ali b. al-Hakam from Hisham b. Salim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
The Qur’an that Jibril عليه السلام came with to Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله was seventeen thousand verses
